notes.liver: The largest solid organ. It lies in the right upper abdomen under the right dome of the diaphragm, protected by the lower ribs. It makes bile, and the gallbladder sits on its under-surface.
notes.spleen: Lies in the left upper abdomen, behind the stomach and against the diaphragm, under ribs 9–11. It filters the blood; it can be injured when the lower left ribs are broken.
notes.pancreas: Lies across the back of the upper abdomen, behind the stomach. Its head sits in the C-shaped loop of the duodenum and its tail reaches the spleen. It makes digestive enzymes and insulin.
notes.kidney_right: Lies on the back wall of the abdomen (retroperitoneal), beside the spine. It usually sits a little lower than the left kidney because the liver lies above it.
notes.kidney_left: Lies on the back wall of the abdomen (retroperitoneal), beside the spine, slightly higher than the right kidney. Its renal vein crosses in front of the aorta to reach the inferior vena cava.
notes.gallbladder: A small pear-shaped sac on the under-surface of the liver. It stores and concentrates bile, which reaches the duodenum through the bile ducts.
notes.stomach: A J-shaped organ in the left upper abdomen, below the diaphragm, between the oesophagus and the duodenum. Its size and shape change a lot with filling.
notes.aorta: The main artery of the body. In the abdomen it runs down in front of the spine, a little to the left, and divides into the two common iliac arteries at about the level of L4.
notes.inferior_vena_cava: The large vein that carries blood from the lower body to the heart. It runs up on the right side of the aorta and passes behind the liver to the right atrium.
notes.esophagus: The muscular tube from the throat to the stomach. It passes behind the heart and goes through the diaphragm at about the level of T10.
notes.duodenum: The first part of the small intestine, curved like a 'C' around the head of the pancreas. Bile and pancreatic juice enter it.
notes.urinary_bladder: Lies in the pelvis, behind the pubic bone, and stores urine. On CT its size depends on how full it is.
